stem: Which of the following is NOT a form of data erasure?

options.explanation: Clearing refers to the overwriting of data media intended to be reused in same organization. Purging refers to degaussing or overwriting media intended to be removed from the organization.

Purging applies a qualifying method to make recovery infeasible even with advanced laboratory techniques. Purging refers to degaussing or overwriting media intended to be removed from the organization.
Clearing sanitizes user-addressable media against simple recovery through normal system interfaces. Clearing refers to the overwriting of data media intended to be reused in same organization.
Destruction sanitizes by rendering the media unusable for its former storage purpose. Destruction refers to completely destroying the media.

explanation.summary: Clearing refers to the overwriting of data media intended to be reused in same organization. Purging refers to degaussing or overwriting media intended to be removed from the organization.
